text:
jia: heads up — noticed a sharp drop in prefix-cache hit-rate for a small cohort of customers starting ~2026-03-14 :eyes:. baseline was ~78-82% for redwood-2.1-large on /chat/completion, now down to ~52-58% for some tenants (ACME, BetaCorp).

alex: whoa, that's a big delta. any coincident changes? kernel roll last week + batching tweak on Thursday. could be related.

maria: confirmed timelines — kernel-selector v2.3.8 rolled 2026-03-12, batching heuristic change (windowed batching fallback) deployed 2026-03-13.

sam: can you paste the dashboard slice?

jia: attaching the quick query we used to produce the tenant timeseries (sampled):
```
-- cache_metrics table
SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) as h, model, route, tenant,
  sum(tokens_saved) as tokens_saved, count(*) as requests,
  avg(cache_hit::int) * 100.0 as hit_pct
FROM cache_metrics
WHERE model = 'redwood-2.1-large' and route = '/chat/completion'
  and ts >= '2026-03-10'::timestamptz
GROUP BY h, model, route, tenant
ORDER BY h;
```

riley: quick findings from that: ACME's hit_pct dropped from 80% --> 55% starting 2026-03-13 07:00 UTC, tokens_saved/day down ~60M. BetaCorp similar but smaller. Other tenants unchanged.

ops-bot: deploy v2.3.8 kernel-selector deployed by @infra-bot at 2026-03-12T02:14Z

alex: hypothesis 1 — kernel change exposed a perf regression that pushed long-seq requests into slower scheduling lanes which altered batching timing. if batching includes an affinity bucket id in the cache key (or changes normalization), that can break keying. check key derivation.

maria: looked at key derivation — we do include a deterministic "exec_profile" tag that used to be stable, but kernel-selector now annotates profile with a kernel_hint (e.g. "k:v2" vs "k:v3") which got included in the final key string. that seems... problematic.

sam: so the same logical prompt can have two different cache keys depending on kernel hint meta. that would explain the misses. is kernel_hint semantically required in key?

riley: no, it was originally temporary during rollout. 2.3.8 accidentally left the annotation on. I can reproduce locally: same prompt, identical tokens, but key hash differs when kernel_hint present.

jia: good catch. what about warmup and prefetch paths — do they normalize keys the same way?

maria: prefetch path used normalize=true so it strips most runtime annotations, but the fast-path warmup (used by Dedicated customers) was using a lighter normalizer and kept exec_profile intact — so warmup misses too.

alex: action items: (1) patch kernel-selector to stop emitting kernel_hint into exec_profile (or mark it ephemeral) (2) add a defensive filter in key-normalizer to drop runtime-only annotations (3) add a dashboard panel for hit-rate by kernel_version & by batch_size so we detect this earlier.

sam: agree. also recommend a short-term mitigation: add a fallback that looks up canonical key (without exec_profile) when a miss occurs and increment a "retro-hit" metric if it succeeds. cheap and will recover tokens while we rollout the fix.

jia: low-cost telemetry to add now: retro_hit_count, retro_hit_tokens_saved, miss_reasons tagged with key_components. put them into the cache_metrics stream.

riley: i'll open a PR to strip kernel_hint from exec_profile and roll a hotfix. timeline: PR now, canary in ~2 hours, full rollout 3-4 hours if no regressions.

maria: i'll add a quick Grafana panel: heatmap of hit_pct by kernel_version (x) vs batch_size (y) and a time series overlay for tokens_saved/day. also a by-tenant table sorted by delta.

alex: small note on batching interaction — the new windowed batching increases observed inter-arrival variance and can cause more batch_size=1 cases for short tail tenants, which also reduces prefix-sharing opportunities. please include batch_size distribution in the dashboard.

sam: good call. also add sampling for raw prompt fingerprints on misses (only 0.1% sample) so we can validate whether prompts are actually different or keying is at fault. store sampled fingerprints in private S3 for privacy.

jia: can someone put a short-runbook for this? we should include rollback criteria and token-saved impact thresholds.

riley: drafting runbook:
- If retro_hit_tokens_saved/day > 30M for a tenant -> immediate hotfix rollout to strip exec_profile
- If canary shows any increase in P99 latency above 5% -> pause and investigate
- If overall hit_pct recovers to within 5% of baseline within 12 hours -> close incident

ops-bot: alert created: "prefetch.keying.regression" severity=warning, notify=eng-runtime on-call

maria: quick note—we should also add an analytic that attributes token-saved delta to: keying changes vs batching vs kernel latency. approximate by running an A/B on canary vs previous kernel on a small tenant slice.

alex: agreed. final ask: add an automatic daily digest that surfaces top 10 tenants by tokens_lost_due_to_cache_regression. put in #eng-runtime-ops weekly briefly.

jia: thanks all. riley please ping when PR is merged and canary is green, i'll keep watching the ACME slice and post updates here. :thumbsup:

riley: PR merged and canary started at 2026-03-14T15:22Z. first 2h looks okay — retro-hit metric already reporting ~45M tokens recovered across canary tenants. continuing rollout.
